title: "ADR: mighty_complete_study() class"
date: "2026-11-02"
author:
  - "Aksel Thomsen"
---

## Status

|             |                                                    |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Package     | mighty.metadata                                    |
| Version     | 0.1.0                                              |
| Description | New complete metadata class to ease downstream use |

## Success criteria

1. Users can easily specify simple predecessors. Both column predecessors such as `ADXX.MYVAR` (currently supported) and predecessors from supplementary domains and BDS parameters should be supported.
1. Metadata is used consistently for code generation and documentation, in {mighty} and {mighty.toolbox} respectively, without any further processing inside the two packages.
1. Information from components is re-used as much as possible, so users do not have to create redundant specifications.

## Context

Currently, the main export of {mighty.metadata} is the `mighty_study()` class that defines all ADaM metadata for a study.
It is sparsely defined so that users do not have to specify redundant information, which makes the current class
suitable for CRUD updates, but not suitable for downstream use.

It has the following helper functions to alleviate this:

1. `resolve_includes()`
1. `resolve_subsets()`
1. `populate_core()`
1. `populate_sparse()`

They have to be called appropriately in all integrations.

To make this easier, this ADR proposes a new class that handles this consistently,
and also adds functionality to inherit metadata from the referenced components.

## Decisions

Create a new `mighty_complete_study()` class that holds the resolved `mighty_study()` object as a property.
It does not inherit from `mighty_study()`.
It populates and resolves all information, ensuring that all metadata and components are directly available for downstream use.

The new flow in the packages becomes:

```
mighty_study()
└─> mighty_complete_study()
    ├─> mighty::generate_adam_code()
    └─> mighty.toolbox::generate_define_xml()
```

Add new downstream methods for both generics, and keep existing `mighty_study()` methods as wrappers:

```
generate_adam_code(<mighty_study>)
└─> mighty_complete_study()
    └─> generate_adam_code(<mighty_complete_study>)

generate_define_xml(<mighty_study>)
└─> mighty_complete_study()
    └─> generate_define_xml(<mighty_complete_study>)
```

The new `resolve_components()` helper is exported alongside the existing helpers.
All helper functions consistently return a `mighty_study()` object.

The `populate` argument of `mighty_study()` is soft-deprecated in favor of `mighty_complete_study()`.
It only runs `populate_core()` and `populate_sparse()`, and skips includes and subsets.

## Consequences

Downstream use in {mighty} and {mighty.toolbox} has to be updated after this feature is released.

Any new special `mighty_*` components have to be added to {mighty.standards}.

{mighty.metadata} adds {mighty.component} to `Imports`.
There is no circular dependency, since {mighty.component} does not depend on {mighty.metadata}.
{mighty.standards} is not a package dependency. It is a GitHub repository of components, found through the `repos` field in `_mighty.yml`.

### Changes to current content

1. Update `populate_sparse()` to write the parsed predecessor reference to `component.id` and `component.with`. `method` is kept unchanged.
1. The `mighty_study()` object then has direct references to the special `mighty_*` components.
1. The `populate` argument of `mighty_study()` is soft-deprecated.

## Alternatives Considered

### 1. Only add a new helper function to resolve components and inherit component metadata

Not chosen, because a separate class guarantees that downstream code receives a fully resolved object,
and lets {mighty} and {mighty.toolbox} dispatch on it.
With only a helper, every integration must call it, and nothing ensures that it was called.

### 2. Handle supplementary data as part of the base domain specification

Proposed as Option A in [mighty#95](https://github.com/NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty/issues/95).
The base domain gets a flag, and columns refer to `SUPP` only.
The SUPP-- data set is derived from the base domain (e.g. `AE` --> `SUPPAE`):

```yaml
population:
  base:
    - domain: AE
      include_supp: TRUE

columns:
  - id: AETECH1
    method: SUPP.AETECH1
```

This keeps the two-part `DOMAIN.COLUMN` notation, and with multiple base domains
(e.g. LB and XL) one column entry can get values from both SUPPLB and SUPPXL.

Not chosen, because it requires changes to `population`, makes `SUPP` a reserved domain name,
and only supports SUPP-- data sets of the base domain. Instead, we use the explicit
`SUPPDM.EFFICACY.QVAL` notation, which maps directly to a predecessor with a where clause
and needs no flag on the base domain.

## Implementation Details

In general, this change should be implemented in many smaller increments to ensure we
continuously remain compatible with {mighty} and {mighty.toolbox}.

Proposed implementation order:

1. Update `populate_sparse()` to support component predecessor mapping. Extend the predecessor regex in `populate_sparse()` and `is_predecessor()` to accept the three-part `DOMAIN.VALUE.COLUMN` notation.
1. First version of `resolve_components()`.
1. Add any new special `mighty_*` components to {mighty.standards}.
1. First version of `mighty_complete_study()`, only implementing component metadata re-use. Note that this means {mighty} will temporarily fetch the components a second time.
1. Implement the new method dispatch in {mighty} and {mighty.toolbox} to ensure compatibility. Combined with the above changes, this marks the initial complete implementation. The changes below are for optimization and further streamlining.
1. Remove now-redundant logic around predecessors in {mighty}.

### Component metadata retrieval

The component metadata is added in the following steps:

1. After `populate_sparse()`, all predecessor columns have `component.id` and (if needed) `component.with` entries.
1. A new `resolve_components()` function populates component tags back to the `column` entries in the `mighty_study()` object:
   1. `@origin` --> `column.origin`
   1. `@method` --> `column.method`
1. The rendered component objects are stored in `@nodes` of `mighty_complete_study()` (see below).

`resolve_components()` uses the `repos` field of `_mighty.yml` (`@mighty`) to find standard and local components.
If `@mighty` is `NULL`, it returns the study unchanged. This supports documentation-only use.

Fields are only filled when missing. Precedence is user > predecessor > component:

1. `origin`: user, else `"Predecessor"`, else component `@origin`.
1. `method`: user, else component `@method`.
1. `component`: user, else the shorthand mapping.

Every helper, and the full pipeline, must give the same result when run again on its own output.
This is needed because the `generate_*(<mighty_study>)` wrappers always call `mighty_complete_study()`,
and a resolved `mighty_study()` cannot be distinguished from a raw one.

### `mighty_complete_study()`

This is a new S7 class with parent `S7_object`, with all specifications explicit.
It holds the study as a property rather than inheriting from `mighty_study()`.
Unlike `mighty_study()`, the specifications must now be read-only.

This cannot be ensured in the underlying `<list>` parent of `mighty_study()`.
Instead, the complete study specifications must be stored as a property in the object.
Proposed structure with all properties as read-only:

```
<mighty_complete_study>
@ properties :
  $ spec       : <mighty_study>  # The resolved and populated study specification
  $ components : <list>          # Named list with all components used in the study
  $ nodes      : <list>          # Nested list of nodes, see below
```

Read-only is enforced with set-once setters.
Each setter only allows the assignment at construction, and errors afterwards:

```r
spec = S7::new_property(
  class = S7::new_union(NULL, mighty_study),
  default = NULL,
  setter = function(self, value) {
    if (!is.null(self@spec)) {
      cli::cli_abort("{.field @spec} is read-only")
    }
    self@spec <- value
    self
  }
)
```

Rendered components are R6 objects and are not protected from in-place modification.
The guarantee is that `@spec`, `@components` and `@nodes` are consistent with each other at construction.

`mighty_complete_study(x, ...)` passes `...` on to the helpers (e.g. `info` to `resolve_includes()`).
`@spec` is built with:

```r
x |>
  resolve_includes(...) |>
  resolve_subsets() |>
  populate_core() |>
  populate_sparse() |>
  resolve_components()
```

`@nodes` has a package-neutral structure owned by {mighty.metadata}; downstream packages adapt to it.
Each node has `type` (column, row, or parameter), `id`, and `component` (the rendered component object):

```
@nodes$ADSL$AGE
  $ type      : "column"
  $ id        : "AGE"
  $ component : <mighty_component_rendered>
```

### Predecessor mapping and components

To ensure a good user experience, we want to support shorthand notation for simple predecessor mapping.
Assuming our current domain is `ADSL` and the base domain is `DM`, the different predecessor types can be mapped as follows:

1. Keep column from the base domain:
   `id: MYVAR` --> `component.id: mighty_init_domain` with `component.with.domain: [DM]`
1. Rename column from the base domain:
   `method: DM.DMSEQ` --> `component.id: mighty_col_rename`
1. Copy existing column into new column:
   `method: ADSL.MYVAR` --> `component.id: mighty_col_mutate`
1. Join predecessor from other domain:
   `method: ADXX.VAR2` --> `component.id: mighty_col_echo`
1. Join predecessor from supplementary SDTM data:
   `method: SUPPDM.EFFICACY.QVAL` --> `component.id: mighty_merge_supp`
1. Join predecessor from ADaM BDS data set:
   `method: ADVS.BMIGRP.AVALC` --> `component.id: mighty_merge_param`
1. Join predecessor from SDTM findings data:
   `method: VS.SYSBP.VSSTRESN` --> `component.id: mighty_merge_param`

In case 1, a column with no `method` and no `component` is taken from the base domain(s).
Several base domains are row-bound, and all must have the column.
`origin` is set to `"Predecessor"` if missing.

`populate_sparse()` parses the `method` shorthand into a structured `component.with` with `domain`, `column`, and optional `filter`.
`method` keeps the user's shorthand unchanged, so the predecessor source is available for define.xml.
Example for a column in `ADAE` (case 4):

```yaml
# input
- id: AGE
  method: ADSL.AGE

# after populate_sparse()
- id: AGE
  method: ADSL.AGE
  origin: Predecessor
  component:
    id: mighty_col_echo
    with:
      domain: ADSL
      column: AGE
```

The three-part notation `DOMAIN.VALUE.COLUMN` filters the predecessor domain on `VALUE`.
The filter key is derived from the domain prefix:

1. `SUPP--`: `QNAM`
1. Domain in the study (ADaM BDS): `PARAMCD`
1. Any other domain (SDTM findings): `<DOMAIN>TESTCD`

```
SUPPDM.EFFICACY.QVAL  -> filter QNAM     = EFFICACY
ADVS.BMIGRP.AVALC     -> filter PARAMCD  = BMIGRP
VS.SYSBP.VSSTRESN     -> filter VSTESTCD = SYSBP
```

The filter is stored in `component.with`, e.g. for SUPP--:

```yaml
component:
  id: mighty_merge_supp
  with:
    domain: SUPPDM
    column: QVAL
    filter:
      QNAM: EFFICACY
```

Metadata inheritance for three-part references:

1. ADaM BDS (`ADVS.BMIGRP.AVALC`): inherit from the `AVALC` column of parameter `BMIGRP` first, then from the `AVALC` column of `ADVS`.
1. SUPP-- and SDTM: the source is not in the study, so users must specify label and type.

{mighty.metadata} only passes domain, column and filter in `component.with`.
Components choose their own join keys (e.g. `USUBJID`, or `IDVAR`/`IDVARVAL` for SUPP--).

The first four components are already implemented in {mighty}, and the standard components exist in {mighty.standards}.
`mighty_merge_supp` and `mighty_merge_param` have to be written. Potentially, they can be combined into one.
This is decided during implementation.

Open question: whether the case 1 mapping stays inside {mighty} for performance.
If so, this is an exception to success criterion 2.

With this change, all components must have correct `@method` and `@origin` tags, which is not the case for the existing components.

## Testing Strategy

1. Keep all tests for exported functions in downstream packages the same, ensuring a consistent user experience.
1. Only remove internal tests when the functionality is made redundant by this new class.
1. Run integration tests against {mighty} in the {mighty.metadata} CI. Run integration tests against {mighty.toolbox} in the {mighty.toolbox} CI, since it is an internal repository.
1. Add unit tests in {mighty.metadata} for:
   1. Parsing of the two- and three-part predecessor notation, including the filter key rules.
   1. Field precedence (user > predecessor > component).
   1. Each helper and `mighty_complete_study()` give the same result when run again on their own output.
   1. Read-only properties of `mighty_complete_study()`.
   1. `resolve_components()` returns the study unchanged when `@mighty` is `NULL`.

## Risks

Internally, {mighty} handles a lot of the logic that is now pushed forward into the component helpers.
Depending on how large the required changes are, we may have to plan them separately from this document.

## Compliance Considerations

None.
